summary.answer:
The answer depends on whether we consider the global customer base or just the US, as all 10 distribution centers are located in the United States:

1. **Globally:** The single largest cluster of customers is located in **Beijing, China** (1,554 users). The closest distribution center to this cluster is in **Los Angeles, CA**, which is approximately 10,067 km away.
2. **Within the US:** The largest cluster of domestic customers is in the **New York area** (666 users). The closest distribution center to this cluster is the **Port Authority of New York/New Jersey NY/NJ**, which is just about 25 km away.

I've mapped both scenarios for you. The map shows global customer clusters (colored by user density) alongside the 10 US-based distribution centers (black points), with the major clusters and their corresponding closest distribution centers annotated.

tools.name: run_sql

input.sql:
WITH user_h3 AS (
  SELECT
    `carto-un`.carto.H3_FROMGEOGPOINT(ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude), 4) AS h3,
    COUNT(*) as user_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users`
  GROUP BY 1
),
largest_cluster AS (
  SELECT
    h3,
    user_count,
    `carto-un`.carto.H3_CENTER(h3) AS cluster_centroid
  FROM user_h3
  ORDER BY user_count DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
centers AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    name,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude) as geom,
    latitude, longitude
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.distribution_centers`
)
SELECT
  l.h3,
  l.user_count,
  ST_X(l.cluster_centroid) as cluster_lon,
  ST_Y(l.cluster_centroid) as cluster_lat,
  c.name as nearest_dc_name,
  c.latitude as dc_lat,
  c.longitude as dc_lon,
  ST_DISTANCE(l.cluster_centroid, c.geom) as distance_meters
FROM largest_cluster l
CROSS JOIN centers c
ORDER BY distance_meters ASC
LIMIT 1;
